title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: Let \(N\) be the positive integer \(7777\ldots777,\) a \(313\)-digit number where each digit is a \(7.\) Let \(f(r)\) be the leading digit of the \(r\)th root of \(N.\) What is \[ \begin{aligned} &f(2)+f(3)+f(4)\\ &\quad{}+f(5)+f(6)? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
The number \(N\) satisfies \[7\cdot10^{312}\lt N\lt 8\cdot10^{312}.\] Multiplying or dividing by a power of \(10\) only shifts the decimal point, so we only need the leading factor left after taking out the largest convenient power of \(10.\)

For \(r=2,\) \(\sqrt N\) has leading factor between \(\sqrt7\) and \(\sqrt8,\) so \(f(2)=2.\)

For \(r=3,\) the leading factor is between \(\sqrt[3]{7}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{8},\) so \(f(3)=1.\) For \(r=4,\) the leading factor is between \(\sqrt[4]{7}\) and \(\sqrt[4]{8},\) so \(f(4)=1.\)

For \(r=5,\) since \(312=5\cdot62+2,\) the leading factor is between \(\sqrt[5]{700}\) and \(\sqrt[5]{800}.\) Since \(3^5\lt700\lt800\lt4^5,\) \(f(5)=3.\)

For \(r=6,\) the leading factor is between \(\sqrt[6]{7}\) and \(\sqrt[6]{8},\) so \(f(6)=1.\) The sum is \(2+1+1+3+1=8.\)

Thus, the answer is A .
hints: For each root, factor out the largest power of \(10\)
